extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) guidance for examination of patent applications, focusing on searches, requirements for information (37 CFR 1.105 / 1.59), handling informal or incomprehensible disclosures, evidentiary criteria for nonobviousness, and expungement/handling of trade-secret materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority and main conditions for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination authority arises under 35 U.S.C. 131; main conditions precedent to grant are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 131 directs the Director to cause an examination to be made; 35 U.S.C. 101 states that whoever invents/discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter (or improvement) may obtain a patent, subject to conditions and requirements of title. Use form paragraph 7.04 which copies 35 U.S.C. 101. (Context: examiner must evaluate application in light of these statutory standards.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of the application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is assigned, the examiner must review contents to determine if the application meets the requisites of 35 U.S.C. 111(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check matters affecting filing date or abandonment (oath/declaration, filing fee, claims). Ensure application meets MPEP Chapter 600 requisites as to formal matters and completeness/clarity of disclosure. If requisites are not met, applicant may be called upon for necessary amendments; such amendments must not include new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling obviously informal cases (MPEP §702.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure when application disclosure is informal or insufficient so that a complete action on the merits is impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps the examiner may follow: (A) make a reasonable search of the invention as it can be understood; if disclosure is so incomprehensible that a reasonable search cannot be made, inform applicant no search was made; (B) note informalities and drawing deficiencies via attachments to the Office action; (C) require that the specification be revised to conform to idiomatic English and U.S. patent practice; (D) reject claims as failing to define the invention per 35 U.S.C. 112 if they are informal (blanket rejection usually sufficient). If many informal claims, treat them as a single claim for fee/examination purposes. Encourage applicant to submit a preliminary amendment (preferably within 3 months) correcting obvious informalities; do not allow new matter in such amendments. Examiner should attempt to point out points of informality and may request correlation of terminology with art-accepted terminology (use form paragraph 7.01 where terminology prevents a proper search).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unconventional terminology — cannot be examined (form paragraph 7.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If terminology used is so different from art-accepted terms that a proper prior-art search cannot be made, the application cannot be properly examined until clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require applicant to provide clarification or correlation with art-accepted terminology; caution applicant not to introduce new matter; set a shortened statutory reply period (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer). Examiner notes: fill in specific problematic terminology/units/pages in bracketed form paragraph text. See MPEP §702.01 which nonetheless requires a reasonable search where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure incomprehensible — objection under 37 CFR 1.71 (form paragraph 7.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If disclosure is so incomprehensible as to preclude a reasonable prior-art search, object under 37 CFR 1.71 and require amendment to clarify the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request amendment clarifying the disclosure so the examiner can properly compare with prior art; warn applicant not to introduce new matter; set shortened statutory period for reply; indicate pages/features not understood in bracketed paragraph; use appropriate form paragraphs for rejection of claims when necessary; see MPEP §§608.02(a),(b) for drawing informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search requirements (MPEP §704.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading specification and claims, the examiner searches the prior art; the invention should be thoroughly understood before searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching subject matter covered in MPEP Chapter 900 (esp. §§904–904.03). Informal or imperfectly understood cases are nevertheless given a search to avoid piecemeal prosecution. When assigned after another examiner's action, give full faith and credit to prior examiner's search and action unless there is a clear error or knowledge of other prior art—second examiner generally should not reorient the approach or perform a new search merely to find something different. See MPEP §719.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 — authority and illustrative examples (MPEP §704.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner or Office employee may require from inventors (37 CFR 1.56(c) individuals) or assignees such information as may be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat a matter in a pending/abandoned application or reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in 37 CFR 1.105(a)(1)(i)-(viii) include: (i) particularly relevant commercial databases known to inventors that could be searched; (ii) whether a prior-art search was made and what was searched; (iii) copies of non-patent literature/published applications/patents by any inventor relating to the claimed invention; (iv) copies of literature used to draft the application; (v) copies of literature used in the invention process (designing around/providing a solution); (vi) identification of what is being improved (for improvements); (vii) identification of any use of the claimed invention known to inventors at filing time; (viii) technical information known to applicant concerning related art, disclosure, claimed subject matter, or accuracy of examiner’s interpretation. Presentation formats may include a requirement for factual information, interrogatories (specific questions), or stipulations. A reply stating the information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted as a complete reply. Replies and failures to reply are governed by §§1.135 and 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: What information may be required — reasonable necessity and factual limitation (MPEP §704.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information may be required only if it is reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter and there must be a reasonable basis for the information requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 places a substantial burden on applicant that should be minimized by clearly focusing the reason and scope of the expected response; scope should be narrowly defined and a reasonable basis must exist. The regulation seeks factual information (facts known to applicant or readily obtainable after reasonable inquiry), not opinions. Applicant need not derive or independently discover facts (e.g., by experimentation) in response. The purpose is to improve patent quality and not to place applicants in jeopardy regarding duty of candor/good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for requiring information to find prior art (MPEP §704.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information necessary for finding prior art is justified where the information is reasonably necessary to the examination or treatment of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable necessity is generally met where: (A) the examiner’s search and preliminary analysis shows the claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class or keyword among patents and typical non-patent literature sources (e.g., new technology area lacking classification), or (B) the application file or lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner’s search justifies asking the applicant whether they have relevant information (e.g., applicant-authored documents or scarce art indicates applicant likely has knowledge). In such cases, applicant may be among the most knowledgeable about areas of search; requiring applicant’s input is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific types/examples of information that may be reasonably required (MPEP §704.11(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exhaustive list of particular factual items the examiner may request when reasonably necessary for examination or finding prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) name/citation of any particularly relevant indexed journal or treatise; (B) trade name(s) of goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; (C) citation/dates/copies of advertising/promotional literature for goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; (D) citation/copies of journal articles describing such goods/services; (E) trade names/providers of competing goods/services; (F) written descriptions/analyses prepared by inventors/assignees of competing goods/services; (G) identification of pending/abandoned applications filed by at least one inventor or assigned to the same assignee that disclose similar subject matter and are not identified in current application; (H) reply to matters raised in a 37 CFR 1.291 protest; (I) explanation of technical material in a publication (including inventor’s publications); (J) identification of changes in reformatted continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (K) a mark-up for a continuation-in-part showing added subject matter where there is an intervening reference; (L) comments on a new Federal Circuit decision that appears on point; (M) publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant that may qualify as printed publication prior art; (N) comments on whether information of record raises derivation issues under 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (O) art related to applicant’s invention/disclosure/claimed subject matter; (P) other factual information pertinent to patentability; (Q) accuracy of the examiner’s stated analysis; (R) clarification/correlation for means-or-steps-plus-function claim support (35 U.S.C. 112); (S) interrogatories or stipulations about claim features/support/meaning/utility/public use facts etc. (specific interrogatory topics 1–9 are listed in the MPEP). These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making a requirement for information (MPEP §704.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information is discretionary and may be made when a necessity is recognized; timing affects utility of the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimum time is prior to or with the first action on the merits because examiner has maximum opportunity to consider and apply the response; ordinarily do not make a request with or after a final rejection. A requirement may be appropriate prior to first action (e.g., restriction requirement) when search/preliminary analysis shows claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class/keyword or in emerging tech areas with minimal prior art. Factors to consider before a separate requirement prior to first action include: (A) claimed subject matter in newly established art area; (B) whether applicant submitted an IDS; (C) whether specification’s background adequately describes background; (D) whether related documents authored by inventor/assignee not submitted are found during search; (E) whether non-patent literature is referred to but copy not supplied; (F) whether background describes information as known/conventional but unfamiliar to examiner and not findable by search. Requirements may also be made in abandoned applications or patents in proceedings such as revivals, change of inventorship, or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to a requirement for information (MPEP §704.12 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: How replies to requirements for information are handled and limits on combining such requirements with office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement for information may be combined with a first action on the merits that includes at least one rejection when justified by application file or lack of relevant prior art. It is not appropriate to make a requirement for information with a first-action allowance or Ex parte Quayle action. Replies that state the requested information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted as complete replies. Replies (and failures to reply) are governed by 37 CFR §§1.135 and 1.136; see MPEP for definitions of complete/incomplete replies, treatment of incomplete replies, and time periods for reply. The requirement’s format and examiner obligations following applicant’s reply are addressed in MPEP §§704.14 and 704.14(a)-(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of requirement for information to duty of disclosure and candor
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for factual information are distinct from (but related to) applicant’s duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56) and duties of candor/good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.105 seeks facts known to applicant or readily obtainable after reasonable inquiry and is not intended to request opinions. Purpose is to improve patent quality and render better decisions, not to put applicants in jeopardy of meeting duties of candor and good faith in replies. Examiner should narrowly focus requests and have reasonable basis for requiring information. See MPEP §704.12(a) for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence of nonobviousness and related evidentiary criteria (MPEP §716)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and considerations for objective (secondary) evidence of nonobviousness: nexus, probative value, weighing, and categories of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General applicable criteria include: (A) objective evidence of nonobviousness (categories listed), (B) nexus requirement and evidence of nexus between claimed invention and secondary considerations, (C) probative value of objective evidence, and (D) weighing objective evidence in overall obviousness analysis. Specific guidance: evidence must show unexpected results (716.02(a)); burden on applicant to provide such evidence (716.02(b)); examine and weigh evidence of expected results vs allegations of unexpected results (716.02(c)); unexpected results must be commensurate in scope with the claimed invention (716.02(d)); compare with closest prior art (716.02(e)); advantages may be disclosed or inherent (716.02(f)); use appropriate declaration/affidavit form (716.02(g)). Commercial success must be commensurate in scope with the claimed invention (716.03(a)) and derived from the claimed invention (716.03(b)). Other secondary considerations include long-felt need and failure of others, skepticism of experts, copying, inoperability of references, utility/operability of applicant’s disclosure, sufficiency of disclosure, and attribution. See MPEP §716 for tests and weighing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials and Information Disclosure submissions (MPEP §724 and §724.02–.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for submitting, handling, and protecting trade secret/proprietary materials and for papers submitted in the file wrapper; types of materials, sealing, and office handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes methods of submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective order materials (including sealed envelopes), types of materials that may be submitted under MPEP §724.02, and Office treatment/handling. Materials submitted in an application covered by 35 U.S.C. 122, reissue applications, and reexamination files have particular open-to-public rules under 37 CFR 1.11(b)/(d). Applicants should identify material that may later be subject to request by placement in a separate sealed envelope/container; unidentified material may inadvertently be placed in Office prior art search files and may not be retrievable. See MPEP §724 for more on completeness of file wrapper and submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to expunge information from application file (37 CFR 1.59; MPEP §724.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and procedure for petitioning to expunge information (other than original disclosure) from the application file under 37 CFR 1.59(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information forming part of the original disclosure (specification including claims, drawings, preliminary amendments in executed oath/declaration) will not be expunged. An applicant may request expungement of other information by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) with required fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) and establishing to the Director’s satisfaction that expungement is appropriate. The decision on such a petition is typically held in abeyance until allowance, Ex parte Quayle action, or abandonment, at which time a Technology Center Director decides (subject to particular conditions). Expungement is appropriate when petitioner complies with criteria in MPEP §724.05 and the examiner determines the information is not material to patentability. If information was inadvertently submitted, specific factors (MPEP §724.05, II) apply. If petition is granted, expunged material must be retained by petitioner for life of any patent issuing on the application. Form paragraphs 7.204–7.213 provide sample grant/dismissal and specific dismissal reasons, including: lack of fee, information considered material to patentability, information made public, no commitment to retain information, no clear statement that information is trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order or was unintentionally submitted, unclear identification of information to be expunged, or petition not submitted by/for the party in interest who originally submitted the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and clarity of examiner’s action and required content in Office actions (MPEP §707.07 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the content and clarity of examiner’s actions (office actions) to ensure proper prosecution and record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should provide complete action on formal matters, require new oath when appropriate, follow draftsperson’s requirements, use proper language when rejecting claims, note all outstanding requirements, and answer all material traversed by applicant. Piecemeal examination should be avoided. Each claim should be mentioned in each office action and the action should state when claims are allowable. Other procedural guidance includes numbering paragraphs, notifying inaccuracies in amendments, reviewer/assistant initialing, signing by authorized examiner, entry and mailing dates, and handling returned office actions. See the MPEP subparagraphs for form paragraph usage and more detailed instructions.
